findings.trigger: 200 or error headers followed by partial never-ended response below 1MiB; caller expiry or thread interruption during send/body receive.
findings.actualStaticProof: A single nanoTime deadline is created once, using min(15 seconds, remaining authentic caller session expiry); request timeout and asynchronous get use remaining budget. BoundedResponse future completes only on EOF, failure or rejection. Non-200 subscription cancels without draining. Timeout/interruption yields code-only UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; finally cancels unfinished exchange, closes response subscriber, then closes owned request input and secret. Synchronized request read and close fence original-array access before erasure. Late handler stores subscriber then observes stopped; either handler sees stopped or finally sees its stored subscriber. A late onSubscribe sees closed and cancels. Growth arrays, accumulator and EOF result are explicitly erased.
findings.currentRuntimeProof: Current gate-2 XML: all five GuidedSecretByteBodyTest invocations pass, including original complete200/503 controls, mTLS partial200, partial503, interruption and default15s. Actual owned request array and SecretValue char array are inspected after exit; one physical POST, client certificate and peer disconnect are asserted. No joined consume/read/recovery proof is inferred.

findings.trigger: Exact1MiB accepted body or 1MiB+1 rejection; timeout/cancel racing delayed body handler/onSubscribe/onNext; cleanup after parse/schema/identity failure; request read racing close.
findings.actualStaticProof: Source limits accumulation before copying each chunk, erases replaced growth arrays, and erases accumulator plus EOF-result in synchronized close. Closed request input blocks late reads and clears original under same monitor. Existing tests retain exact request/char references and observe server disconnect, but do not capture response-owned accumulator/result arrays or deterministically race late subscribers/publisher reads. Tests use <3000ms for1s deadline and <16000ms for15s default, so they do not independently measure a strict caller-expiry clamp with tight tolerance. Server dribbles whitespace every20ms; fully silent body-after-headers is covered by source logic, not a distinct runtime case.
findings.exactReversibleRepair: Add bounded private seam tests retaining exact accumulator/replaced/result references, controlled late handler/subscription and synchronized read/close interleavings. Assert zero arrays/no post-close original read, cancellation/no new dispatch, exact cap behavior, silent partial-body and malformed/schema/identity controls. Record monotonic network-budget timing against configured clamp with explicit scheduler tolerance; keep all completebody controls. Do not claim library/parser copy erasure or a hard wallclock15s method-return guarantee.

deadline.staticProof: GuidedMaterializationService copies authentic session expiresAt. Nonsecret dispatch passes won.context.expiresAt; secret dispatch reads current secretSession expiresAt and passes it to sendSecret. Deadline=min15s/caller expiry is converted once to nanoTime. remaining never resets. Async exchange future includes EOF/body subscriber completion; future.get uses remaining after serialization/request creation. Expired/interrupted checks prevent fresh send; InterruptedException restores flag. No response-header-only input stream remains.
deadline.scopeLimit: This is a configured transport budget for request and receive-body wait. Token supplier performs regular mounted-file Files.readString; local serialization, parsing/schema validation, monitor cleanup and scheduler latency are not independently preempted. Remaining checks after parse/validation refuse late success. No claim of hard15s whole-service execution (which includes PG/Vault) or exact15s wallclock method return.

cancellation.staticProof: finally sets stopped before cancelling unfinished exchange and fetching subscriber. Handler first stores subscriber then checks stopped, covering both late-handler orderings. close synchronizes against onNext/onComplete, erases arrays, then cancels subscription; late onSubscribe sees closed and cancels. Nested finally still erases owned request and chars if cancellation throws. Request read/close use same monitor; after close any read throws before touching original bytes.
cancellation.callerCancellationLimit: Thread interruption is real tested caller cancellation. Public session cancel/revocation/expiry commits monotone stop and asynchronously sends existing stop control; it does not directly interrupt an already waiting sender via a new cancellation registry. The original sender stays bounded by15s/session expiry. Do not equate transport interruption test with timed public revocation or protected-page teardown.

requestOwnership.original: SecretWireWriter returns exact serialized byte[] passed into OwnedRequestBody; test observer keeps that original. SecretValue.Writer writes char[] directly and erases it in finally; sendSecret also closes on all exits. Owned read(byte[],off,len) copies into JDK targets while holding the same monitor used by zeroing close. Original never becomes a published ByteBuffer.
requestOwnership.jdkCopies: Actual gate Java21 RequestPublishers.StreamIterator allocates obtains a separate buffer, calls is.read(buf,offset,capacity), and publishes that buffer. These transient copied HTTP/TLS/OS buffers are not owned arrays this code can erase. Cancellation fences future original reads; it cannot erase copies already delivered to JDK/network.

responseOwnership.arrays: Initial4096 accumulator grows only to1MiB; predecessor filled zero during synchronized growth. onComplete copies exactly count into result; final subscriber.close zeroes both current accumulator and result before cancellation. Timeout/size/reject/onError/parse/schema/identity failures all traverse finally. A late subscriber is closed before subsequent accepted read.
responseOwnership.immutableAndLibraryResiduals: Incoming JDK ByteBuffers are transport-owned. GuidedContracts.parseWire decodes an immutable String and builds JsonNode/parser state; these copies and Jackson/decoder/TLS buffers are not explicitly zeroed. A hostile response echo could reach those transient parser copies; no all-copy erasure or all-sink canary guarantee is inferred from mutable-byte-array cleanup.
responseOwnership.runtimeLimit: Exact request/char arrays tested; response growth/result/late-race arrays presently static only.

consumeAndRecovery.staticProof: consume forbids ambient transaction, locks exact session/owner/source/admission, saves DISPATCHING/dispatchCount1 and historical command in TransactionTemplate before returning WonConsumption. AlreadyConsumed cache stores ledger only, never authority; valid duplicate returns ledger before resolve/send. active check precedes duplicate path: terminal UNKNOWN/CANCELLED/EXPIRED refuses before new read/send. Dispatch resolves only winner, records actual resolution/version before sender, and closes Resolved. Timeout/error UNKNOWN carries no raw failure cause/body; session lostAcknowledgment preserves committed callback if already terminal or action notDISPATCHING. HTTP200 alone is not a callback. stop maps unresolved DISPATCHING action to existing UNKNOWN_OUTCOME/ACK_LOST; ACK_LOST label alone proves no actual ack-loss cut. Existing stop control is not a secret resend.
